summary: Terminal AI coding agent from Charm that works with many LLMs, keeps per-project sessions, and uses LSPs and MCP servers for extra context.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Crush is an AI coding assistant for the terminal. It connects your code, tools and workflows to the LLM you choose, lets you switch models mid-session without losing context, keeps multiple sessions per project, uses language servers (LSPs) for code context, and can be extended with MCP servers over http, stdio or sse.
sixtySeconds.problem: Gives you a polished terminal coding agent that isn't tied to one model provider and runs on almost any OS.
whoFor: Developers who live in the terminal
People who want to choose or switch LLM providers
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for multi-model support, LSP-aware context, MCP extensibility and first-class support on macOS, Linux, Windows, Android and BSDs.
requirements: A model provider: Charm Hyper, an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini and others, or a local model

overview: Install with Homebrew, npm, Winget, Scoop, Arch, Nix or FreeBSD packages, then run crush in your project.

The quickest start is picking a Charm Hyper model in the model picker and signing in. Or press ctrl+l, choose another provider and paste your key, or set environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY.
Configuration covers themes, LSPs, MCPs, hooks, skills, tool permissions and custom or local providers. It is licensed under FSL-1.1-MIT.
